title: firmware: main.c cannot start REST API — auth_handler required but no auth component exists
description:
## What is wrong
Commit eca31a3 added a fail-closed check in rest_api_start() at
rest_api.c:283-286 that requires config->auth_handler != NULL. This is
correct security policy.

However, main.c:47-50 initializes rest_api_config_t with only .port
and .status_provider — auth_handler is NULL (zero-initialized). Since
no auth component exists yet (evb-1gp.8 is still open), rest_api_start
always returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG and the firmware boots with no
working HTTP server.

This blocks all end-to-end testing, device-level tests, and any
incremental development on REST API endpoints.

## Where
- firmware/main/main.c:47-50 — api_config missing auth_handler
- firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c:283-286 — NULL check

## Fix options
a) Add a development-only stub auth handler in main.c that always
   returns ALLOW, guarded by a Kconfig option or a compile flag
   like CONFIG_EVB_RELAY_DEV_NO_AUTH
b) Implement the real auth component (evb-1gp.8) to unblock this
c) Temporarily relax the NULL check to allow NULL = allow-all
   (reverts the fail-closed fix)

Suggested: (a) — keeps fail-closed in production, unblocks dev/test.
close_reason: Resolved by wiring the real auth component into main and REST API startup

title: Device test suite still fails mod_io and rest_api cases after watchdog verification
description:
A live `just test-device` run on 2026-03-18 completed under the new whole-run watchdog in 230.51s, so the watchdog path itself worked as intended.

The suite still failed on existing Unity/device cases that are unrelated to the watchdog wrapper:
- `mod_io device relay readback matches writes`

- `rest_api device enforces the SSE client limit`

pytest-embedded also logged `unity test case not found, probably due to a timeout` warnings while processing the full menu-driven run.

Why this matters:

- The failing cases cluster around MOD-IO relay readback plus REST API SSE/auth behavior, so they should be debugged as firmware/device-test bugs rather than as tooling failures.

Acceptance criteria:

- Fix the underlying firmware or test-app issues so the listed Unity cases pass again.

notes: 2026-03-21 investigation narrowed this bead further: a live rerun showed case 31 (rest_api device emits SSE heartbeats) now passes, so the surviving reproduced failure is case 10 only (mod_io device relay readback matches writes). Focused serial repro of case 10 failed at firmware/test_app/main/test_mod_io_device.c:104-108 because mod_io_set_relays(0x05) was followed by a readback of 0x00. The official Olimex MOD-IO manual does not document any 0x40 relay-read command, which directly conflicts with the repo's newer authoritative-readback model. Follow-up bug filed to reconcile the project contract with primary-source docs and live hardware before continuing this bead.

title: cli: TOML config file silently ignores unknown keys — typos cause silent misconfiguration
description:
## What is wrong
loadFile in cli/internal/config/config.go:200 calls
toml.DecodeFile(path, &decoded) and ignores the returned MetaData.
The BurntSushi/toml library's MetaData.Undecoded() method returns
TOML keys that were present in the file but not mapped to any struct
field.

A user who writes api-token (hyphen) instead of api_token (underscore),
or who misspells api_tokn, gets NO error — the key is silently ignored
and they get an 'auth failed' error with no hint that the config file
has a typo.

## Where
cli/internal/config/config.go:199-201

## Fix
Check MetaData.Undecoded() after DecodeFile. If any undecoded keys
exist, return a config.Error{Kind: ErrorKindInvalid} listing the
unrecognized keys. This matches the strict-parsing convention common
in CLIs (e.g., kubectl, terraform).

Example:
  meta, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &decoded)
  ...
  if undecoded := meta.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
      names := make([]string, len(undecoded))
      for i, k := range undecoded { names[i] = k.String() }
      return ..., wrapf(ErrorKindInvalid, "unknown keys in %q: %s",
                        path, strings.Join(names, ", "))
  }

## Impact
Medium — frustrating to debug. User thinks config is applied but it
is silently ignored. Especially common with api_token vs api-token.
close_reason: loadFile now rejects undecoded TOML keys instead of silently ignoring them

title: cli: map raw 403 robot fallback to AUTH_FORBIDDEN
description:
## What is wrong
The robot envelope fallback in cli/internal/robot/errors.go maps a raw HTTP 403 with no structured API code to AUTH_INVALID. The firmware and e2e contract use AUTH_FORBIDDEN for forbidden responses, so unstructured 403 responses are mislabeled in robot mode.

## Why this matters
This makes the CLI less consistent with the firmware contract and with existing e2e expectations. A proxy, stub, or future server path that returns only status 403 without a JSON error code should still surface AUTH_FORBIDDEN.

## Done when
- apiStatusCode maps 403 to AUTH_FORBIDDEN
- robot envelope tests cover the raw 403 fallback path
- just ci passes
close_reason: Completed: raw 403 robot fallback now maps to AUTH_FORBIDDEN and is covered by a regression test.

title: Device test: auth device distinguishes missing and wrong bearer tokens fails
description:
The Unity device test case 'auth device distinguishes missing and wrong bearer tokens' ([auth][device]) is the sole remaining failure in just test-device as of the 2026-03-18 run (228s, 1 failed).

All other previously-failing device cases are now passing after commits 2c03801 (I2C two-call fix), c9c1c73 (recv loop + 16 KB stack), and 83bf5ca (CLI OTA defer close).

Known facts:
- Test verifies REST API returns distinct HTTP 401 (no bearer token) and HTTP 403 (wrong bearer token).
- firmware auth.c / rest_api.c auth path is unchanged in recent commits; failure pre-dates this session.
- Static analysis of rest_api_send_error_internal() shows correct 401/403 guarding.
- Test follows immediately after token generation tests calling device_config_set_api_token(); leftover token state could cause wrong-token path to behave as no-token.

Acceptance criteria:

- Fix applied so the Unity case passes reliably.
- just test-device runs clean with 0 failures.

title: Default test-device watchdog is too low for current hardware suite
description:
Currently the repo-default just test-device watchdog is 180 seconds via EVB_TEST_DEVICE_WATCHDOG_SECONDS, but a live run on 2026-03-19 timed out exactly at that limit after the test app built and pytest-embedded had already started executing the device suite.

title: firmware: production REST API exhausts URI handler slots at startup
description:
## What is wrong
The current production firmware boots, gets an Ethernet lease, then fails to start the REST API with `ESP_ERR_HTTPD_HANDLERS_FULL`. The latest serial log on 2026-03-18 shows:

`W httpd_uri: httpd_register_uri_handler: no slots left for registering handler`
`E main: Failed to start REST API: ESP_ERR_HTTPD_HANDLERS_FULL`

The Tier 3 integration lane now gets through flash and provisioning but cannot proceed to HTTP because the server never finishes registering all handlers.

## Why it matters
This is now the concrete blocker for hardware-backed end-to-end verification after the serial download-mode path was restored. Ethernet and DHCP succeed, but the control plane still does not come up.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Production firmware starts the REST API successfully on hardware
- A regression test covers the URI handler capacity requirement or startup path
- `just ci` passes and Tier 3 progresses past server startup
notes: Captured a fresh production boot log on 2026-03-18 after restoring single-port flashing on /dev/ttyS4. Firmware now reaches Ethernet DHCP successfully, gets IP 192.168.200.211, then fails REST API startup with ESP_ERR_HTTPD_HANDLERS_FULL because URI handler registration exhausts the default httpd slot count.
close_reason: Raised REST API URI handler capacity to match the registered routes, added a regression check, and verified on hardware that the production firmware now starts the HTTP server and the Tier 3 lane progresses through all HTTP cases.

title: SSE event stream silently drops MODIO_PRESENCE events
description:
## What

rest_api_sse_format_message() in rest_api.c (line ~702) handles four of the five event types published by the input monitor:
- EVB_RELAY_EVENT_DIGITAL_INPUT
- EVB_RELAY_EVENT_ANALOG_INPUT
- EVB_RELAY_EVENT_RELAY_CHANGED
- EVB_RELAY_EVENT_BUTTON

It does NOT handle EVB_RELAY_EVENT_MODIO_PRESENCE. The default: case returns false, silently dropping the event.

## Impact

Clients connected to GET /api/v1/events will never learn when MOD-IO hardware appears or disappears from the I2C bus. This is the most important infrastructure event for any automation client — it changes whether relay and input commands will succeed.

## Fix

Add a case for EVB_RELAY_EVENT_MODIO_PRESENCE in rest_api_sse_format_message() that formats a JSON payload like:
  event: modio_presence
  data: {"present":true,"ts_ms":12345}

The event data type is evb_relay_modio_presence_event_t (defined in relay_events.h).

title: Hardware reference hardcodes transient ttyS4 details after warning that guest tty numbers drift
description:
## What is confusing

`docs/hardware-reference.md` correctly warns that guest `/dev/ttyS*` numbering is dynamic under QEMU/virsh and that repo defaults should use stable aliases. But the later "Current Runner Caveat" section still hardcodes transient diagnostics like:
- `/dev/ttyS4` as the guest node
- `./scripts/check-download-mode.sh --port /dev/ttyS4` as the passing example
- `EVB_SERIAL_PORT=/dev/ttyS4 just test-device` as the working invocation

That directly conflicts with the earlier guidance and goes stale as soon as the same runner enumerates the UART as a different tty node.

## Impact

Future sessions are likely to cargo-cult the stale tty path back into commands, docs, or debugging notes even though the stable repo contract is `/dev/esp32-evb`. The document currently mixes a stable policy with unstable examples from one observation window.

## Expected direction

- Keep the dynamic-node observation only as a dated diagnostic footnote if it is still useful
- Prefer `/dev/esp32-evb` in the runnable examples and success claims
- Make the runner-specific section explicitly about the stable PCI match and alias rule, not the transient tty number

## Acceptance Criteria

- Runnable examples in `docs/hardware-reference.md` use stable aliases instead of a transient `/dev/ttyS*` path
- Any retained tty-node observation is clearly marked as historical/debug-only, not an operational default
- The doc no longer contradicts its own guidance about dynamic guest tty numbering

title: MOD-IO single-relay setters trust cached state instead of hardware readback
description: In mod_io.c, mod_io_set_relay and mod_io_toggle_relay use s_state.relay_mask directly instead of calling mod_io_read_relay_mask_locked(). This violates the requirement in initial-plan.md to perform an authoritative read-modify-write cycle against the hardware, which can cause silent state corruption.

title: Use-after-complete API violation in rest_api_events_handler error paths
description:
In `firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c`, `rest_api_events_handler` detaches the HTTP request using `httpd_req_async_handler_begin(req, &async_req)`. However, if subsequent steps (such as allocating buffers or launching the task) fail, the code invokes `httpd_req_async_handler_complete(async_req)` and then incorrectly attempts to send an error response using the original `req` pointer via `rest_api_send_error(req, ...)`.

According to ESP-IDF documentation, using `req` after beginning an async handler violates the API contract. Sending data after completing the async handler creates a use-after-free/use-after-complete condition that can lead to crashes or socket corruption.

Fix: Either respond using `async_req` before completing it, or perform all necessary resource allocation and validation before transitioning the request into async mode.
close_reason: Fixed rest_api_events_handler so every post-detach SSE setup failure responds on the async request copy, completes ownership exactly once, and leaves the client slot clean. Added device regression coverage for forced task-start failure after async detach. Verified with just format and just ci; attempted just test-device on /dev/esp32-evb, but execution is currently blocked before case enumeration by evb-20mx (corrupted Unity menu line / pytest_embedded parse failure).

title: MOD-IO device tests fail with ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT on I2C probe
description:
All 6 MOD-IO device tests fail with 'Expected 0 Was 263' (ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT=0x107).

- mod_io_probe() uses a timeout that is too short relative to test app I2C bus init timing

title: cli: AUTH_FORBIDDEN from firmware not in robot error policies — missing 403 remediation hint
description:
## What is wrong
The firmware sends `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` as the error code for 403
responses (rest_api.c:96). But the CLI's robot error policy map
in errors.go:99 and the capabilities contract in capabilities.go:91
use `AUTH_INVALID` (matching the plan's Step 12c, not the firmware).

When the CLI receives a 403 from the firmware:
1. apiErr.Code = "AUTH_FORBIDDEN" (from firmware JSON)
2. buildErrorDetails sets details.Code = "AUTH_FORBIDDEN"
3. knownErrorPolicies()["AUTH_FORBIDDEN"] → not found
4. No remediation hint set in robot envelope
5. Agent gets no "Provide a valid API token via..." message

Meanwhile, 401 responses with AUTH_REQUIRED are correctly matched
and get the remediation hint.

The integration test (pytest_integration.py:107) acknowledges the
mismatch by checking for both:
  assert code in {"AUTH_REQUIRED", "AUTH_FORBIDDEN"}

## Fix options
a) Add AUTH_FORBIDDEN to knownErrorPolicies and capabilities
   ErrorCodes, keeping AUTH_INVALID as an alias
b) Change the firmware to use AUTH_INVALID on 403 (matching the plan)
c) Update the plan to use AUTH_FORBIDDEN and remove AUTH_INVALID

Suggested: (a) — maps both codes, handles whatever the firmware sends.
Add to errors.go knownErrorPolicies:
  "AUTH_FORBIDDEN": {Retryable: false, Remediation: stringPtr(authRemediation)}
Add to capabilities.go ErrorCodes:
  "AUTH_FORBIDDEN": {ExitCode: 3, Retryable: false, Remediation: stringPtr(authRemediation)}
close_reason: Completed

title: MOD-IO relay-state readback contract conflicts with official manual and live hardware
description:
The repo currently treats command 0x40 as authoritative MOD-IO relay-state readback and uses it in firmware, tests, and docs. A focused hardware rerun on 2026-03-21 shows that assumption is not holding on the deployed board: Unity case 10 (mod_io device relay readback matches writes) still fails because mod_io_set_relays(0x05) is followed by a 0x40 readback of 0x00.

Primary evidence:
- Focused device rerun on 2026-03-21 for case 10 failed at firmware/test_app/main/test_mod_io_device.c:104-108.
- Captured serial output: after "Detected MOD-IO at 0x58; relay mask refreshed to 0x00", the board still reported 0x00 after a write of 0x05.
- The official Olimex MOD-IO user manual (MOD-IO.pdf, section 2.7) documents 0x10, 0x20, 0x30-0x33, and 0xF0, but does not document any relay-read command.
- Repo history shows the plan originally stated that no 0x40 relay-read command exists (commit f15e206), and later docs/code were changed to assert the opposite (commit c43491a / e20b764).

Why this matters:
- main.c currently calls mod_io_probe() from app_status_provider(), so if 0x40 is not a real relay-state source, authenticated status/header paths can report wrong MOD-IO state at runtime.
- Device/host tests and docs are currently encoding a hardware contract that the live board does not satisfy.

Done when:
- the project has one authoritative MOD-IO relay-state contract that matches the deployed hardware and primary-source docs
- firmware, host tests, device tests, and docs are aligned to that contract
- evb-35l is either narrowed or closed against the corrected contract

title: SSE disconnected-release path leaves orphaned client task invisible to shutdown force-release
description:
When rest_api_sse_client_task() detects a dead socket via
rest_api_sse_client_connection_alive(), it calls
rest_api_sse_release_disconnected_client_slot(). This function
clears the client slot (active=false, task_handle=NULL) BEFORE
completing the async request. Between the slot clear and the
async completion + vTaskDelete(NULL), the client FreeRTOS task
is still alive but invisible to rest_api_sse_stop()'s
force-release loop (which only acts on active slots).

If rest_api_sse_stop()'s 15-iteration wait loop times out while
the client task is still in httpd_req_async_handler_complete(),
rest_api_stop() proceeds to call httpd_stop(), tearing down the
HTTP server while the orphaned task still holds a reference to
httpd structures — a use-after-free.

The timing window is microseconds and the wait budget is 3.75-15s,
so this is unlikely in practice, but the code is not
correct-by-construction.

Possible fix: keep active=true and task_handle set in the
disconnected-release path until after async completion, or track
orphaned task handles in a separate list for the shutdown to join.

File: firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c
Functions: rest_api_sse_release_disconnected_client_slot (line 893),
           rest_api_sse_stop (line 1357), rest_api_stop (line 3779)
close_reason: Completed

title: SSE force-release can delete client task mid-cleanup, leaking async HTTP request
description:
Race condition between rest_api_sse_release_client_slot (client task teardown) and rest_api_sse_force_release_client_slot (shutdown).

Sequence:
1. Client task enters release_client_slot, takes local copies of queue/req, NULLs them on client, unlocks
2. Frees queue, then calls httpd_resp_send_chunk + httpd_req_async_handler_complete on req

Meanwhile in sse_stop after 15s drain timeout:
1. force_release sees client->active=true but queue=NULL, req=NULL
2. Takes task_handle (still set, release hasn't memset yet), calls vTaskDelete
3. httpd_req_async_handler_complete never executes, leaking the async request

Fix: Set client->active = false under lock immediately after taking local copies in release_client_slot, before unlock. force_release then sees active=false and returns early.
close_reason: Fixed in commit a07b19b (fix(firmware): keep SSE client lifetime alive until async request completes). The release function now keeps the slot active until httpd_req_async_handler_complete() returns.

title: rest_api: queue and async req leak if force_release kills task during cleanup
description: If `rest_api_sse_force_release_client_slot` kills the client task after the task has already entered `rest_api_sse_release_client_slot` and transferred ownership of `req` and `queue` to its local stack variables, but before it actually frees them, then the task is terminated and `force_release` (seeing NULL fields) also skips freeing them. This causes a memory leak of both the FreeRTOS queue and the ESP-IDF async request handle. A possible fix is to not kill the task if `req == NULL`, allowing the task to finish its graceful teardown.
close_reason: Won't Fix

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
TOON FORMAT — Why and How:

TOON (Table-Oriented Object Notation) is the default robot output format because:
1. Lower token count than JSON for tabular data (relay lists, input arrays)
2. Human-scannable (indentation-based, no brackets/braces)
3. Spec-compatible parsers exist for agent consumption

The encoder must handle these specific shapes:
- Status: nested object (uptime, firmware_version, network.*, modio.*)
- Relay list: uniform object table (relays[6]{group,id,state,sync}: ...)
- Input list: uniform object table (inputs[4]{id,state}: ...)
- Config: flat object (poll_interval_ms: 200, hostname: esp32-evb-relay)
- Error envelope: nested with optional fields

CONFORMANCE: The encoder MUST pass upstream TOON conformance fixtures before shipping. A non-conformant encoder would break any agent using a standard TOON parser.

The encoder is OUTPUT-ONLY — we never need to parse TOON. The CLI produces TOON; agents consume it. If an agent prefers JSON, they use --robot --format json.

title: Robot envelope — Wrap() for TOON/JSON output with error mapping
description:
Structured envelope wrapper for all non-streaming robot mode output.

## What
- cli/internal/robot/envelope.go: Robot envelope struct + Wrap() function
- cli/internal/robot/errors.go: error -> remediation mapping table
- cli/internal/robot/context.go: DeviceContext from response headers
- Envelope fields: v (1), command, timestamp, elapsed_ms, exit_code, host, device_context, data (success) or error (failure), warnings, next[]
- robot.Wrap(cmd, w, WrapOpts{Data, DeviceContext, Err, Format}) handles:
  - Building the envelope from command metadata + client response
  - Error -> remediation mapping for real API/device conditions
  - Populating next[] suggestions when the firmware provides a useful next action
  - Marshaling to TOON or JSON based on Format
  - On non-zero outcomes: returns typed error with exit code (after envelope is written)
- Root command must intercept the typed error so Cobra doesn't print a second human error line

## Why
The robot envelope is the CLI's machine-readable contract. Agents parse it to understand results, errors, and suggested next actions. Centralizing envelope construction in Wrap() ensures every command produces consistent, well-formed output.

## Considerations
- Wrap() writes the envelope to stdout, THEN returns a typed error — the error is only for setting the exit code, not for additional output
- Do not preserve remediation flows that only existed to recover from the obsolete MOD-IO unknown-state model
- The envelope version (v:1) is pinned — version bumps are breaking changes
- input watch is the one explicit exception that does NOT use the envelope (uses NDJSON instead)
close_reason: Completed

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
DESIGN RATIONALE — Robot Envelope:

The robot envelope serves multiple purposes:
1. STRUCTURED ERRORS: Agents parse error.code (not human messages) to decide next actions
2. REMEDIATION: error.remediation contains a command template showing how to fix the problem
3. DEVICE CONTEXT: device_context (from firmware response headers) gives agents hardware state without a separate status call
4. NEXT ACTIONS: next[] suggests follow-up commands based on current state
5. TIMING: elapsed_ms enables latency monitoring

The typed exit error pattern is important: robot.Wrap() writes the envelope to stdout, then returns a typed error carrying the exit code. The root cobra command intercepts this error type and calls os.Exit() without Cobra printing its own error message. This prevents double-printing errors (once in the envelope, once by Cobra's default error handler).

The envelope version (v:1) is pinned. If the schema changes in a backward-incompatible way, v must be bumped, and agents must check v before parsing.

title: Relay commands — list, on, off, toggle, set
description:
CLI commands for relay control — the primary user-facing feature.

## What
- `evb-relay relay list`: list all relay states + MOD-IO sync metadata
- `evb-relay relay on <target>`: turn relay on (for example `onboard:1`, `modio:3`)
- `evb-relay relay off <target>`: turn relay off
- `evb-relay relay toggle <target>`: toggle relay
- `evb-relay relay set <targets...>`: multi-target batch (for example `onboard:1=on modio:all=off`)
- Target format: `<group>:<id>` where group is `onboard` or `modio`, id is 1-based
- Each command handler: calls client, then dispatches to `robot.Wrap()` or `format.Output()`
- `relay set` batch: coalesce MOD-IO targets into a single bulk PUT, report per-target results
- Partial failure: `exit_code=1`, `error.code=PARTIAL_FAILURE`, per-target `ok/error`, `all_ok=false`

## Why
Relay control is the core purpose of the entire system. These commands are what users and automation agents use most frequently.

## Considerations
- Target parsing must validate group names and ID ranges (`onboard:1-2`, `modio:1-4`)
- `relay set` should coalesce MOD-IO targets into ONE bulk PUT because the firmware protocol is full-bitmap and batching avoids transient intermediate states
- Because firmware can read current MOD-IO state authoritatively, partial MOD-IO target sets may fill unspecified relays from device state instead of requiring an all-4 recovery command
- The batch result format reports per-target success/failure even though the MOD-IO targets share a single bulk request outcome
- If firmware reports `MODIO_NOT_PRESENT (503)`, surface the hardware-unavailable error directly
notes: Starting CLI relay commands after confirming just ci is green locally on 2026-03-18; remaining QA critical path is blocked by runner download-mode hardware outside the repo, so this is the next productive code-local bead.
close_reason: Implemented relay list/on/off/toggle/set with MOD-IO batch coalescing, partial-failure reporting, and CLI regression tests. just ci passed on 2026-03-18. Remaining blocker is the external runner download-mode QA gate, not missing CLI behavior.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
DESIGN NOTES — Relay Set Batch and MOD-IO Coalescing:

When a user runs: evb-relay relay set modio:1=on modio:3=off onboard:1=on

The CLI must:
1. Parse all targets into a desired-state plan
2. Group by transport: MOD-IO targets → one bulk PUT, onboard targets → individual PUTs
3. For MOD-IO: build the full 4-relay bitmap. If only modio:1 and modio:3 are specified but modio:2 and modio:4 are not, the CLI needs to decide: error (require explicit all-4 specification) or use current known state for unspecified relays. Current plan: require all 4 if MOD-IO sync is unknown; allow partial if synchronized (fill from device state).
4. Send the bulk MOD-IO PUT + individual onboard PUTs
5. Report per-target results even though MOD-IO targets share a single request outcome

PARTIAL FAILURE: If the onboard PUT succeeds but the MOD-IO PUT fails (e.g., 409 MODIO_STATE_UNKNOWN), the batch result shows per-target ok/error. The exit code is 1 (general) with error.code PARTIAL_FAILURE.

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text: Design correction: MOD-IO relay batching still matters because the firmware protocol is full-bitmap, but the 409 recovery flow is obsolete. CLI planning should assume authoritative readback is available for unspecified relays when the board is present.

title: modio:all / onboard:all shorthand in relay set
description:
Expand :all shorthand in relay set commands to individual relay targets.

## What
- relay set resolves modio:all and onboard:all into a desired-state plan before choosing transport
- modio:all=off → desired MOD-IO bitmap [false,false,false,false] → one bulk PUT
- onboard:all=on → onboard:1=on, onboard:2=on → two individual onboard requests
- If a single relay set mentions ANY modio:* targets, coalesce into one final 4-relay bitmap and send exactly one bulk MOD-IO request
- Relay count (4 MOD-IO, 2 onboard) is hardcoded to match hardware spec
- Batch results in robot mode still report per-target success/failure

## Why
Convenience for the common case of setting all relays in a group to the same state. The coalescing behavior is critical for MOD-IO: transient intermediate states between separate single-relay writes would be incorrect.

## Considerations
- modio:all is resolved client-side, not server-side — the CLI knows the hardware topology
- The coalescing into a single bulk PUT is mandatory, not an optimization — it ensures clean unknown→synchronized transitions
- Mixed commands like 'relay set modio:all=off onboard:1=on' must send one bulk MOD-IO PUT + one onboard PUT (not 4+1 individual requests)
notes: Starting shorthand expansion after relay command base implementation and green just ci on 2026-03-18.

## What

- evb-relay input analog: list all 4 analog input values (10-bit) + sample metadata
- evb-relay input analog <id>: single analog input
- Each handler calls client, dispatches to robot.Wrap() or format.Output()
- Handles 503 MODIO_NOT_PRESENT and 503 MODIO_SAMPLE_UNAVAILABLE errors

## Why
Input monitoring is the read-side complement to relay control. Digital inputs detect physical switches/sensors; analog inputs measure voltages (e.g., temperature sensors, potentiometers).

## Considerations
- Sample staleness is displayed to the user so they know how fresh the data is
- MODIO_SAMPLE_UNAVAILABLE is retryable (exit code 7) — the device just hasn't polled yet

title: ci: .gitignore missing general __pycache__/ pattern — integration test bytecache would be committed
description:
## What is wrong
.gitignore has path-specific __pycache__ entries:
  firmware/test_app/__pycache__/

But the new firmware/test_integration/ directory also has __pycache__/
with .pyc files that would be committed on `git add`:
  firmware/test_integration/__pycache__/conftest.cpython-313.pyc
  firmware/test_integration/__pycache__/pytest_integration.cpython-313.pyc
  firmware/test_integration/__pycache__/conftest.cpython-313-pytest-9.0.2.pyc
  ...

Any future Python directory (scripts, tools, etc.) would have the
same problem.

## Fix
Replace the path-specific entry with a global pattern at the top
of .gitignore:
  __pycache__/

This is the standard Python .gitignore pattern (used by GitHub's
default Python gitignore template) and catches all Python bytecache
directories regardless of location.

title: firmware: mod_io_set_relay calls probe_locked instead of ensure_present_locked — unnecessary I2C overhead
description:
## What is wrong
mod_io.c:400 — mod_io_set_relay calls mod_io_probe_locked() which
unconditionally performs an I2C probe + relay readback on every call.

mod_io.c:385 — mod_io_set_relays calls mod_io_ensure_present_locked()
which skips the probe if the device is already known to be present.

This inconsistency means every single-relay set (the common operation
from PUT /api/v1/relays/modio/{id}) pays a redundant I2C round-trip
even when the MOD-IO is already present and synchronized.

## Why it matters
At 100kHz I2C, a probe (write 0x40, read 1 byte) takes ~0.5ms. For
interactive relay control this is negligible, but for automated
sequences toggling relays rapidly, the overhead adds up.

## Fix
Change mod_io_set_relay line 400 from mod_io_probe_locked() to
mod_io_ensure_present_locked(), matching mod_io_set_relays.
close_reason: Completed

title: cli: redundant closeFirmwareUpload inside client.New error handler contains dead code
description: In `cli/cmd/ota.go` inside `runOTAFlash`, the code schedules `defer func() { _ = closeFirmwareUpload(firmware) }()`. Right after, if `client.New` returns an error, it manually calls `closeFirmwareUpload` again, checking `if closeErr := closeFirmwareUpload(firmware); closeErr != nil && err == nil`. Since we are already inside `if err != nil`, the `err == nil` check is impossible, making the error assignment dead code. Additionally, since the file handle is already deferred to be closed and `closeFirmwareUpload` is idempotent (it sets `firmware.File = nil`), this manual close block should just be removed to simplify the error handling.
close_reason: Removed the redundant manual closeFirmwareUpload call from the client.New error path because runOTAFlash already defers the file close, and added a CLI regression test that exercises client initialization failure after opening a real firmware file.

title: Split Unity summary line won't match in _collect_case_result_after_prompt

Because buffer only contains the newly read bytes, if a Unity summary line is split across the boundary between the original initial_buffer and the new buffer, the regex will never match since it doesn't see the combined string. 2. just test-integration: ConnectTimeout on first HTTP request after flash due to missing HTTP readiness check in test fixtures (see evb-2huj)

- Justfile (ci-full recipe)
- See evb-2b0q and evb-2huj for underlying issues

Fix both blocking issues:

title: GitHub Actions CI missing firmware host tests (Tier 1) and golangci-lint local recipe

## What

Two gaps between the QA plan and the actual CI pipeline:

### 1. No Tier 1 firmware host tests in CI

The CI workflow (ci.yml) has a firmware-build job but no job to run
the CMake/Unity host tests (just test). The QA plan specifies that
just ci runs format-check + build + test, and the local just ci
recipe does include test. But GitHub Actions only builds.

This means firmware logic regressions (relay, mod_io, input_monitor,
OTA, device_config, main startup) are only caught locally, not in CI.

### 2. No local golangci-lint recipe

CI runs golangci-lint via golangci-lint-action, but there is no
Justfile recipe to run it locally. Developers cannot reproduce lint
failures without manually installing and running golangci-lint.

## Impact

- Firmware host test failures could merge undetected
- CLI lint failures cannot be reproduced locally

## Fix

1. Add a firmware-test job to ci.yml that runs cmake + ctest in the
   esp-idf-ci-action container (or a separate job with just cmake).

2. Add a cli-lint recipe to the Justfile:
     cli-lint:
         cd cli && golangci-lint run --timeout=5m
   And add it to the ci recipe.

title: Stack overflow in main task during rest_api device tests
description:
The firmware crashes with a main-task stack overflow during the device test case `rest_api device reports absent MOD-IO on relay routes` in `firmware/test_app`.

What we know from the current investigation:
- The crash happens after case 22 starts and after board/relay initialization logs appear.
- The expected `REST API server started on port 18091` log line never appears, so the overflow is likely in the case-22 startup path before or during `rest_api_start()`.
- The decoded backtrace only confirms the overflow path through `panic_abort`, `esp_system_abort`, and `vApplicationStackOverflowHook`; it does not yet identify the exact overflowing frame.
- The test app currently sets `CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=16384`, so we should not blindly increase the stack without measuring headroom or removing stack-heavy locals first.
- Earlier rest_api device cases also show `Expected Non-NULL` failures and should be rechecked after the crash is fixed, because they may share the same setup pressure or expose a second bug.

This issue should track the actual firmware fix, not only the host-side timeout behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduction is stable enough to debug the case-22 crash without manual recovery steps.
- The investigation measures main-task stack headroom or otherwise identifies the overflowing path around the case-22 setup and rest_api startup flow.
- The fix removes or justifies the stack pressure correctly; increasing CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE is acceptable only with evidence.
- Case 22 no longer panics or reboots the DUT during just test-device.
- The suite progresses past case 22 so the earlier rest_api failures can be re-evaluated as normal test results instead of being masked by the crash.
close_reason: Fixed: added CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=16384 to firmware/test_app/sdkconfig.defaults (commit c9c1c73). Device test suite now runs past case 22 without stack overflow.

title: firmware: reconcile MOD-IO relay readback support with current unknown-state design
description:
## What is wrong
The project sources disagree about whether MOD-IO supports relay-state readback.

Hardware reference says it does:
- docs/hardware-reference.md:65 — `Relay read cmd | 0x40`
- docs/hardware-reference.md:75 — `Read relay state | 0x40`
- docs/hardware-reference.md:104 — verified working readback on 2026-03-16

But the firmware plan and beads still assume there is no readback:
- docs/initial-plan.md Step 4 / Step 7 describes an unknown->synchronized model because the host cannot query relay state
- evb-1gp.4 and evb-1gp.11 descriptions explicitly say there is no relay-state readback command

## Why this matters
If the hardware really supports authoritative relay readback, the current unknown/synchronized/absent model may be unnecessary complexity and could force clients through bulk PUT flows they do not actually need.

If the hardware reference is wrong, then the docs are actively misleading firmware work.

## Needed follow-up
- Verify on hardware whether command `0x40` is authoritative for the deployed MOD-IO board/firmware
- Update docs/initial-plan.md, docs/hardware-reference.md, and affected beads to a single consistent model
- If readback is real, revisit the MOD-IO REST/API design before implementing evb-1gp.11 so we do not bake in avoidable tech debt

title: Firmware: harden REST API SSE shutdown and async request lifetime
description:
## What is wrong

Static analysis of the current SSE shutdown path, cross-checked against
session `019d03cb-9cee-7773-80f5-5d54442a88c9`, shows that the REST API
has an ownership/lifetime bug around async SSE requests.

The observed hardware signature is that `just test-device` can run clean
through case 33, then fail first at:
- `rest_api device stop owns SSE dispatch task deletion`

and later REST API cases fail as fallout.

The primary root cause is that the SSE client slot is cleared too early.
`rest_api_sse_release_client_slot()` zeroes the client struct before the
async request is fully relinquished via
`httpd_req_async_handler_complete()`. `rest_api_sse_stop()` uses the
zeroed client slot as its shutdown-complete signal and then immediately
calls `httpd_stop()`. ESP-IDF's async request contract still expects the
request completion path to run against live server/session state.

That means shutdown can tear down HTTP server internals while an SSE
client task still owns and is completing the async request.

There is also an adjacent shutdown hazard in
`rest_api_sse_force_release_client_slot()`: it zeroes the client struct
before deleting the client task, which creates a race window on
dual-core ESP32 if the task wakes and touches cleared fields.

## Why this matters

This is a control-plane stability bug in the firmware's long-lived event
stream path. It can corrupt or prematurely tear down REST API state
while stopping the server, and it makes the device test lane unstable in
a way that is easy to misdiagnose as test harness or pytest behavior.

## Scope

This epic tracks:
- pinning down and documenting the SSE shutdown ownership model
- fixing the primary async-request lifetime bug
- hardening the force-release path and related teardown invariants
- adding the narrowest useful host-side regression coverage possible
- re-running focused and full device verification once hardware is
  available again

## Initial evidence

- Session: `019d03cb-9cee-7773-80f5-5d54442a88c9`
- Failing device case: `rest_api device stop owns SSE dispatch task deletion`
- Relevant firmware path: `firmware/components/rest_api/rest_api.c`
- Relevant ESP-IDF contract: `httpd_req_async_handler_complete()` must
  be called only after async work is truly done, and it still touches
  server/session state.

## Done when

- the SSE shutdown path has a single, documented ownership model for
  dispatch-task, client-task, queue, and async-request teardown
- host-side regression coverage exists for the bug or for the extracted
  lifetime invariant, whichever is the narrowest clean approach
- `just ci` passes after the firmware change
- when hardware is available again, focused SSE shutdown verification and
  a full `just test-device` rerun both pass without the case-34 cascade
close_reason: Completed the SSE shutdown hardening work: the async lifetime fixes and host regressions are landed, just ci already passed on the firmware changes, and a 2026-03-21 just test-device rerun passed case 36 plus the later REST API and auth/device cases without cascade failures.

title: rest_api: keep SSE client lifetime alive until async request completion finishes
description:
## What is wrong

`rest_api_sse_release_client_slot()` currently clears the SSE client
slot before the async HTTP request has actually been completed.
`rest_api_sse_stop()` then polls `client->active` as if that meant the
client task and async request are fully done, and proceeds to
`httpd_stop()`.

Static analysis against the ESP-IDF async request contract indicates
that this is too early: `httpd_req_async_handler_complete()` still runs
against live server/session state and only then relinquishes the
underlying socket.

## Why this matters

The current shutdown sequence can let REST API teardown race ahead of an
SSE client that is still completing its async request. That matches the
observed device symptom where the first failure appears at case 34 and
later REST API tests fail as fallout.

## Expected direction

- define an explicit ownership model for:
  - client task lifetime
  - async request lifetime
  - queue lifetime
  - client slot visibility to `rest_api_sse_stop()`
- make the stop path wait for real completion, not just a zeroed client
  slot
- only clear or free request/queue state after no task can still touch
  it
- add succinct inline comments documenting the invariant so the next
  teardown edit does not regress it

## Acceptance criteria

- `rest_api_sse_stop()` no longer treats a cleared client slot as proof
  that async request completion is finished
- the SSE client task, async request, and queue teardown order is
  internally consistent and documented
- `just ci` passes after the firmware change
- later hardware verification can re-run case 34 without reproducing the
  shutdown cascade
close_reason: Completed

title: test: add host-side regression coverage for SSE shutdown lifetime invariants
description:
## What is needed

The current host test harness does not exercise `rest_api.c` directly,
so the primary SSE shutdown bug is only visible in the device lane.
That is too expensive and too fragile for an ownership/lifetime bug.

We need the narrowest host-side regression that can lock down the
shutdown invariant without requiring hardware.

## Constraints

- keep the scope narrow; do not build a giant fake HTTP stack unless it
  is actually required
- prefer extracting or isolating a small lifetime helper if that is
  cleaner than making the full `rest_api.c` compile in host tests
- any chosen seam must still prove the real ordering constraint, not a
  toy approximation

## Acceptable outcomes

One of the following is acceptable:
- compile enough of the SSE shutdown path in the host harness to test
  the real code directly, or
- extract a small helper/state transition that captures the async
  request / client slot / queue teardown ordering and test that helper
  under the host harness

## Acceptance criteria

- there is Tier 1 host coverage for the primary SSE shutdown lifetime
  invariant, or for the extracted seam that owns it
- the regression fails against the broken ordering and passes with the
  fix
- the added test strategy is documented inline where the seam is not
  obvious
- `just ci` passes with the new coverage

title: Firmware: preserve SSE async-request lifetime across startup failure paths
description:
## What is wrong

The new `rest_api_sse_lifetime` seam now locks down the steady-state
client teardown paths, but `rest_api_events_handler()` still has two
startup failure exits that bypass it:

- queue allocation failure after a slot is marked active
- client task creation failure after the async request is detached

Both paths call `rest_api_sse_clear_client_slot()` before
`rest_api_sse_send_async_error_and_complete(async_req, ...)` finishes the
async HTTP request. That recreates the same ownership mistake in a
narrower branch: `rest_api_sse_stop()` can observe no active clients
while the async request is still live inside ESP-IDF.

## Why this matters

The main shutdown bug is now covered in Tier 1 host tests, but these
startup-failure paths still violate the same lifetime invariant. They
are rarer than the steady-state shutdown path, yet they leave a hole in
the ownership model and could produce the same class of teardown race
under memory pressure or task-create failure.

## Done when

- startup failure paths keep the slot logically active until the async
  error response has been fully completed, or otherwise use an equally
  explicit lifetime owner
- the chosen flow is documented inline where the ordering is subtle
- host coverage is extended if the extracted seam can exercise this path
  without dragging full `rest_api.c` into the host harness
close_reason: Completed

title: firmware: poll interval validation ranges disagree — Kconfig 50-10000ms vs device_config 10-60000ms
description:
## What is wrong
The poll interval minimum and maximum are defined in two places with
different values:

Kconfig.projbuild:
  range 50 10000     (compile-time menuconfig bounds)

device_config.h:
  #define DEVICE_CONFIG_MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 10U
  #define DEVICE_CONFIG_MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 60000U

The Kconfig range only constrains the compile-time default. The
device_config validation applies at runtime via PUT /api/v1/config.

Problems:
- A runtime value of 10ms passes device_config validation but is
  dangerously low for I2C polling. At 100kHz with multiple
  transactions per poll (relay state, 4 digital inputs, 4 analog
  inputs), a full cycle can easily take 5-10ms. Setting poll_interval
  to 10ms could starve the bus or cause transaction timeouts.
- A runtime value of 30000ms passes device_config but exceeds
  Kconfig's documented maximum of 10000ms.

## Fix
Align the two definitions. The Kconfig range should match
device_config's min/max, or vice versa. Consider raising the runtime
minimum to 50ms (matching Kconfig) since 10ms is impractical for
I2C polling with the MOD-IO protocol.
close_reason: Aligned runtime poll interval validation to the documented 50-10000ms range and verified with firmware build

title: ci: gofmt violations in version.go and root_test.go — CI does not enforce Go formatting
description:
## What is wrong
cli/cmd/version.go and cli/cmd/root_test.go use 4-space indentation
instead of tabs in several functions. gofmt -d shows diffs:

version.go var block:
  -    Version = "0.0.0-dev"   (spaces)
  +\tVersion = "0.0.0-dev"   (tab)

root_test.go TestFormattedVersion + TestDefaultVersionUsesDevSemverFallback:
  -    withVersionMetadata(...)  (spaces)
  +\twithVersionMetadata(...)  (tab)

The rest of both files and all other Go files use tabs correctly.
Introduced in commit 3231b2a.

The CI pipeline (just ci) runs `go vet` and `go test` but not
`gofmt -d`. The pre-commit hook checks C formatting (astyle) but
not Go formatting. So the violation passes undetected.

## Fix
1. Run `gofmt -w cli/cmd/version.go cli/cmd/root_test.go`
2. Add `gofmt -l` check to the Justfile cli recipes:
     cli-fmt-check:
         test -z "$(gofmt -l cli/)" || \
           (gofmt -d cli/ && exit 1)
   And add it to `ci: ... cli-fmt-check`
3. Optionally extend the pre-commit hook's Go section to
   check gofmt on staged .go files
close_reason: Completed: enforced gofmt in ci and pre-commit, fixed staged Go package vet paths, and normalized existing CLI formatting drift

title: cli: variable 'context' shadows imported context package in client/client.go
description:
## What is wrong
In client/client.go:202, `deviceContextFromHeaders` declares:
  context := &DeviceContext{}

This shadows the imported `context` package (used elsewhere in the same file for `context.Context` and `context.Background()`). While it does not cause a runtime bug (the `context` package is not referenced inside that function), it:
- Violates Go naming conventions (effective Go discourages shadowing imports)
- Triggers warnings from golangci-lint's `shadow` and `govet` shadow analyzers
- Makes the code fragile: if someone later adds context.Context usage to this function, they'll get a confusing compile error

## Fix
Rename the local variable to `ctx`, `dc`, or `devCtx`:
  devCtx := &DeviceContext{}

## Impact
Low — lint-only, no runtime effect.

title: LwIP socket leaks in test_rest_api_device.c on TEST_ASSERT failures
description: In firmware/test_app/main/test_rest_api_device.c, helper functions like perform_http_request(), open_http_stream_request(), and perform_partition_upload_request() allocate TCP sockets and then use TEST_ASSERT_* macros to validate behavior before calling close(sock). If any assertion fails, Unity performs a longjmp out of the function, permanently leaking the socket. Because ensure_tcpip_ready() checks that exactly CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS are available at the start of tests, a single assertion failure will cause a cascading failure of all subsequent test cases due to socket exhaustion. Sockets should be tracked in a global/static variable so tearDown() can reliably close them on test failure.

title: WiFi config REST API parser produces inconsistent results depending on JSON key ordering
description:
## What is wrong

The WiFi config update endpoint (PUT /api/v1/config/wifi) in
rest_api_parse_wifi_config_update_request() (rest_api.c:1834)
iterates JSON keys using cJSON_ArrayForEach, which follows
insertion order. The validation logic at line 1887 checks
out_request->credentials_clear, which is only set when the
"ssid" key is processed as null. This creates an
order-dependent behavior:

- {"passphrase": "x", "ssid": null} → silently succeeds
  (passphrase is copied at line 1908, then overwritten at line 1865
  when ssid=null sets credentials_clear=true and clears both fields)
- {"ssid": null, "passphrase": "x"} → returns validation
  error at line 1888 because credentials_clear is already true when
  passphrase is processed

Per the JSON specification (RFC 8259 §4), object member ordering
is not significant. A compliant client, proxy, or serialiser is free
to reorder keys, so the API should produce the same result regardless
of key ordering.

## Impact

Low in practice — most clients send keys in a stable order — but it
violates the principle of least surprise and could cause intermittent
400 errors if any middleware reorders JSON object keys.

## Suggested fix

Decouple the validation from iteration order by collecting all fields
in the loop and validating mutual exclusivity after the loop completes,
similar to how the non-WiFi config parser handles its fields
independently. The post-loop validation at lines 1939-1962 already
does some of this but misses the passphrase+null-ssid case.
close_reason: Completed: WiFi config update validation is now order-independent, with host regression coverage plus passing just ci and just test-device on 2026-03-21.

If one of those files regresses without another watched path changing, GitHub Actions skips the firmware-test job and the regression can merge untested.

So lets expand CI path detection so tools changes trigger the firmware host-test lane.

title: cli: go.mod marks hashicorp/mdns as indirect despite direct import in discover command

  github.com/hashicorp/mdns v1.0.6 // indirect

  "github.com/hashicorp/mdns"

Consider adding a CI check:
  cli-mod-check:
      cd cli && go mod tidy -diff

title: Hardware reference documents non-existent split serial aliases
description:
## What

docs/hardware-reference.md lines 8-10 list three "preferred" aliases
in the board spec header:

  - Preferred single-port alias: /dev/esp32-evb
  - Preferred split flash alias: /dev/esp32-evb-flash
  - Preferred split console alias: /dev/esp32-evb-console

Only /dev/esp32-evb exists. There is one physical UART (PCI slot
0000:00:09.0), one udev rule creating one symlink. The -flash and
-console aliases are fictional — no udev rule creates them, no
hardware exposes two separate serial paths, and the runner section
(lines 93-95) confirms a single adapter.

These non-existent aliases also appear in:
  - Lines 46-48 (Serial Device Naming section)
  - Lines 9-10 (board spec header)

The flashing examples (lines 62-76) show split-port usage via
EVB_FLASH_PORT and EVB_SERIAL_PORT env vars. These env vars work
fine for hypothetical two-UART setups, but the examples use device
paths (/dev/esp32-evb-flash, /dev/esp32-evb-console) that nobody
can actually create with the provided udev rules on the current
hardware.

## Impact

A user reading the board spec thinks three device aliases are
available. When they set up the udev rule and only get /dev/esp32-evb,
it looks like something is broken. The docs create false expectations.

## Fix

1. Remove lines 9-10 from the board spec header — only the real
   alias /dev/esp32-evb belongs there
2. In Serial Device Naming (lines 45-48), state that the current
   setup is single-port only; mention that split-port is possible
   with additional hardware but not the current runner configuration
3. Keep the ENV var examples but note they demonstrate a
   hypothetical split setup, not the default
close_reason: Completed
